newsitem.title: USA: Barr Labs, Duramed hurt by FDA veto.
newsitem.headline: Barr Labs, Duramed hurt by FDA veto.

text.p: Shares of Barr Laboratories Inc, and Duramed Pharmaceuticals Inc, fell on Monday after the FDA rejected their generic forms of Premarin, the estrogen-replacement drug manufactured by American Home Products Corp.
Barr Lab stock tumbled 6-5/8 to close at 43-1/4 and Duramed stock fell 3/8 to a 10-3/8 close, while American Home shares enjoyed a 3-5/8 run-up to close at 70-1/4.
"It's good for American Home Products. It's bad for Duramed and Barr," said Alex Zissson, pharmaceutical analyst with Hambrecht & Quist.

Earlier in the day, the U.S. Food an Drug Administration said that it would not approve generic Premarin at this time because data did not assure that the generic forms had the same active ingredients as the brand name drug.
Premarin comes from the filtered urine of pregnant horses.

"The (generic) companies argue that some constituents of Premarin are at such low levels that they are not really essential. But American Home argues that some of these trace elements are so potent, that you cannot exclude the possibility that they have an effect," Zisson said.
"This puts enormous pressure on Duramed. Duramed put a lot of eggs in one basket," said Hemant Shah, healthcare analyst with HKS & Co.
But Shah was more optimistic about the outlook for Barr.
"I am still confident that Barr can launch the product within a year. The company has secured commercial quantity of delta 8,9 DHES, which is the component of controversy," he said.
"(The FDA action) allows American Home Products to have a monopoly for another year," Shah said.
Premarin was the most prescribed drug in 1996, with Premarin family sales of around $1 billion last year.
Zisson was less sanguine about the outlook for Barr Labs and generic premarin.
"American Home has a tendency to keep finding new constituents of Premarin," Zisson said.
